conceptual.anchor: Provide architectural comparison ... Avoid marketing language. Use engineering differences.

governance.anchor: the HPA's five strongest validation decisions are carried into the core unchanged: Similarity != Identity ... Avacchedaka ... Abhava ... LLM boundary ... deferred mechanisms

lexical.anchor: Similarity =/= Identity ... Do not merge concepts because they sound similar. Validate using: ID, Evidence lineage, Original registration, Validation state

pairs_touching.what_says_this: CO-OCCURRENCE only (2 co-occurrences). No lineage_claims found in either direction via full-row scan, despite the plausible complementary reading (Law 1 defines Identity; the negative boundary catalogs non-identities).
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: A row explicitly deriving the non-identities boundary FROM Law 1's identity definition (e.g. 'the negative boundary is exactly the complement of Law 1's Identity relation') would establish a claim.

rationale_evidence.anchor: LLMs may become more intelligent, but they will still need an epistemic layer.
rationale_evidence.statement: Part 6, the consolidated KnowledgeOS-vs-LLM comparison across 12 capabilities, each mapped to a map anchor: preserve semantic identity (LLM absent) -> INV-KOS-002; maintain epistemic history (LLM absent) -> Revisability-001; provenance/reasoning lineage (LLM weak) -> Reasoning-Provenance-001; contradiction handling (LLM weak) -> Contradiction-001; temporal/recency (LLM weak) -> Temporal family; revision (LLM weak) -> Revisability-001/C-5; authority (LLM weak) -> INV-003/C-1; transparency (LLM weak) -> Reasoning-Separation-001; unknown handling (LLM weak) -> H-ZERO-001/C-10; agent accountability (LLM weak) -> Agent-001; inference validation (LLM weak) -> Vyapti-001; evidence authenticity (LLM weak) -> EvidenceAuthenticity-001.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Coextension without Identity -- Ruling: YES -- constitutional, and KnowledgeOS could NOT exist without it.
rationale_evidence.statement: Special Area C ruling: Similarity != Identity is the identity law's limit case; removing it lets extension->identity at any degree of match, up to perfect coextension, collapsing KnowledgeOS into exactly the similarity engine it refuses to be; 'there is no degree of observable match at which the corruption is absent' (a decisive failure test). Consequence: one of the strongest KERNEL rows -- its deep form (Representation != Identity) carried by law 1; the typed encoding is representation, deferred.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Result: only TWO of the five are fundamental architectural absences -- persistent epistemic identity and historical belief evolution
rationale_evidence.statement: LLM-comparison validation (5 candidates, validated not assumed): persistent epistemic identity -- FUNDAMENTAL ABSENCE (a stateless generative model cannot possess it by construction; scaffolding like RAG cannot grant identity, only look up stored identities); historical belief evolution -- FUNDAMENTAL ABSENCE (generation is stateless, no belief to evolve); provenance preservation, contradiction management, justification accountability -- each a DEGRADATION, not an absence (an LLM can be scaffolded to approximate each, weakly). Conclusion: the constitutional justification rests on exactly the two fundamental absences (mapping to laws 1 and 11), not a general 'LLMs are bad at X' claim.
